Research & Engineering Lineage

SSS-L2 — Canonical Software Maintenance and Evolution

Current scientific findings

Maintenance and evolution asks what change is legitimately needed, what the actual operation changes or preserves, and whether the resulting obligations can be supported over time. A useful change, a permitted action and a worthwhile task are separate conclusions.

This is the current derived account of the separately qualified scientific subject. The full scientific account and four-unit family guide provide its complete reasoning, source qualifications and detailed records. Earlier disclosure labels in the retained historical account below describe its earlier publication cutoff.

A justified difference over time

Maintenance and evolution concerns a software system that continues to matter while its needs, environment, understanding or support conditions change. Its first question is what difference is intended and legitimately required. Its second is what the actual operation changes and preserves. Its third is whether the consequences, consumer obligations, cost and capacity remain supportable. These are different inquiries: classification is useful when it guides a decision, but a universal exhaustive taxonomy does not itself answer them. Accepted report, selected canonical properties.

C001's intended difference and legitimate requirement authority remain distinct from C094's authority to execute an action. One actor may legitimately hold both powers; the distinction does not create a mandatory additional approver. A descriptive observation can show what happened but cannot create a right to require or perform it. Likewise, a candidate that changes something useful may exceed the intended task. Correctly identifying the operational effect and the authority boundary prevents “maintenance” from functioning as an unbounded permission label.

Preservation, transformation and adequacy

The lineage distinguishes five questions that are often collapsed. C030 states the behavior-preservation rule under a declared observer and model. C031 asks whether the transformation rule applies to the actual input and conditions. C032 concerns the transformation engine's implementation. C033 concerns the particular candidate produced. C034 concerns whether doing the task is worth its cost. A program compiling after a change does not establish all five. A valid transformation theorem can survive a faulty engine; a correct engine can be used outside a rule's premises; a behavior-preserving candidate can still be economically unnecessary. Canonical predicates and current interpretation.

A transformation can change operative source while preserving the behavior observed by an explicitly chosen observer. That does not make the operation read-only. It also does not imply preservation under every possible observer. Structural and behavioral dimensions must therefore remain separate. The r4 revisions correct neighbouring accounts and explanation fields without erasing their native raw values, so that an actual structure-changing, behavior-preserving operation can be described accurately.

Transitions, recovery and compatibility

C049 concerns recovery of actual effects, whereas C061 concerns reverting source. A source revert cannot recover information destroyed by a noninjective conversion unless the needed information was retained elsewhere. Reopening the old code path is therefore different from restoring the old system state. A feasible inverse, retained backup, containment, forward repair or legitimate acceptance of residual loss can be the appropriate route. The lineage does not prescribe rollback in every case. Report, state/recovery and compatibility analysis.

Composition, induced properties and alternatives

The current composition contains 83 typed relations and eleven configurations. Four induced canonical properties, C102–C105, sharpen existing failure modes: evidence/action coherence across an actual handoff; selective invalidation when a relevant premise changes; obligations over reachable consequential joint states; and assessment of a combined control arrangement's protection, consumers, continuation and burden. Three other candidates are absorbed by existing meanings and six obligations remain open. These findings do not make a new permanent installation mandatory. A narrower existing practice or direct adequate check can supply the function. Composition qualification.

The eleven configurations preserve meaningful alternatives: a stable unchanged system, a small repair, transformation, staged release, concurrent evolution, incremental migration, a rehearsed quiescent transition, phaseout and custody, bounded automation, learned noncode adaptation, and restricted servicing. The choice depends on the task and premises. An older supported baseline can be adequate; a no-change conclusion can be legitimate; a family-wide migration can be unjustified. A known unmet obligation changes that assessment, while a descriptive change in fashion does not.

Economy, support and end of life

AI-assisted work adds candidate, tool, benchmark, task-alignment, work-outcome and authority distinctions. A benchmark result can support a bounded capability without showing durable net maintainability or unattended lifecycle stewardship. General durable net maintainability C095 and general unattended maintenance C100 remain unresolved. This does not rule out bounded assistance, deterministic tools or useful human-and-tool arrangements. It rejects promotion of a narrower success into an unestablished whole-lifecycle capability.

Read the complete structured scientific records, exact source and review qualifications, and preliminary existing-owner receiving questions. Finite examples and scientific qualification establish neither deployed effectiveness nor native implementation.

Maintenance as a continuing obligation

Maintenance concerns useful existing software, its consumers, the environment and the people and resources able to sustain it. It includes preserving behavior, intentionally changing behavior, restructuring, migration, replacement, restricted support and retirement. Noncode artifacts matter when they affect the real obligation. A document can aid maintenance without transferring the actual ability to maintain. The intended outcome, evidence and capable legitimate actor must fit the task. Historical public intake.

The genealogy contains related lenses rather than one complete taxonomy: purpose and activity classifications, population-level evolution, comprehension and reverse engineering, configuration and refactoring, regression testing, migration, economics and ecosystem support. The canonical reconciliation preserves disagreements and source versions. Its 98- and 74-row ancestor populations are not added to the 105 canonical identities; equal source counts in the ancestors do not imply identical bibliographies. Historical source table · Complete property reader.

The distinctions that make a change assessable

Understanding is not the same as changing. A correct refactoring rule does not prove its implementation correct, its application valid for the actual input, or the resulting candidate correct under an excluded observer. Cleaner structure or a better metric need not improve useful future change. The historical property records retain these distinct bearer, criterion, applicability and economic questions. Canonical properties.

Existing behavior is not automatically desired behavior, and passing tests is not a complete specification. Differential agreement, metamorphic relations and mutation evidence have distinct assumptions. Test selection and prioritisation concern cost or detection timing; they do not change what a pass proves. A direct check or the full relevant suite can be cheaper than an elaborate selector. Evidence should answer the intended change question and preserve the relevant exclusions. Historical public intake, tests and observations.

Recovery follows actual effects. Reverting source may leave data loss, external effects or concurrent changes untouched. Safe coexistence is different from recoverability, and neither alone establishes that a temporary migration is finished. A repair, incremental coexistence, prepared cutover, forward recovery or legitimate scope reduction can be appropriate under different premises. The composition provides branches and feedback, not a compulsory serial pipeline. Historical composition model.

Support, economics and meaningful non-change

Useful non-change is legitimate. Evolution hypotheses are not instructions to grow; age is not a defect; modernization has no benefit merely because it is newer. A proposed intervention must justify its outcome, uncertainty, cost and future support burden. Technical debt is a way to reason about prospective burden and value, not a universally calibrated balance that must be reduced to zero. The beneficiary and cost bearer can differ. Historical public intake, operating idea and economics.

A nominal owner needs willingness, knowledge, access and capacity. A message must reach an appropriate consumer able to act. Deprecation, sunset and archival preservation make different promises; an inactive completed project need not be a failed one. Source retrieval, continued service and historical execution reproduction need different evidence. A popular dependency or a repository label does not establish a feasible support response. Historical canonical support and preservation properties.

AI assistance and automated repair produce candidates and evidence, not self-authorising decisions. Net benefit depends on task alignment, quality, verification cost and consequential outcomes. A review step is not automatically sufficient, and the opposite universal claim that human-only work is superior is also unsupported. Different benchmarks, versions, surveys and selected follow-ups must not be pooled as a single representative experiment. Long-term maintainability benefit and general unattended maintenance remain unresolved historical questions. Historical public intake, automation and unsettled questions.

Composition, adverse records and limits

The historical canonical composition retains four analytically induced criteria: coherence among change, evidence and action; selective invalidation of changed assumptions; continuity over relevant reachable joint states; and proportionality/retirement of combined controls. Their parents and finite failure witnesses are explicit. Existing adequate mechanisms can discharge them; they are not four mandatory new installations or a global optimiser. The corpus preserves rejected claims, ceremonies, a superseded form, contested and unresolved claims, together with open composition questions. Historical composition model · All properties and ancestry pointers.

The canonical reconciliation inspected frozen research records. It did not claim to reread every primary work or reproduce the underlying studies. Historical, formal, empirical and analytical evidence retain separate scopes and dependence. Integrity establishes correspondence and custody, not independent truth. The present historical reader does not turn the later accepted r4 corrections into public material, and it does not derive adoption requirements for IMPLEMENTAUDIT.

Existing receiving responsibility

The already-public R003D maintenance qualification distinguishes source disposition, target interpretation, prepared absorption and actual qualification. Its documented portal example uses an inspected source/consumer relationship to justify source metadata, while a co-change score is only an inspection ranking. The rough Maintenance outline preserves the existing #227 and shared-owner routes, including adequate/no-change and research outcomes.

Problem addressed:

Avoid implementing the wrong change correctly.

Failure mode:

An accepted or executed change does not correspond to a legitimate supported objective, or preservation is silently substituted for an authorised behavioural change.

Mechanism:

State the intended difference, affected obligations, legitimate decision maker and acceptance question before endorsing an intervention.

Trigger context:

A request, discovered defect or environmental pressure proposes changing an existing commitment.

Non trigger cheap path:

A short accepted issue with concrete examples is enough for a bounded low-risk change; reject or defer an unjustified request.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • Decision authority and domain meaning must be established; disputed intent cannot be resolved by test count.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C038

  • ESME-C070

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

A request, discovered defect or environmental pressure proposes changing an existing commitment. Identify whose intended result is changing and distinguish corrective, adaptive, perfective, preventive, additive and emergency dimensions without forcing exclusivity.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Change request, affected behaviour and requirements history. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.

Preservation obligation and observer

Those entitled to request or rely on the behaviour, not merely the test author. A request owner or affected stakeholder supplies legitimate intent; observation of existing behaviour alone cannot authorise its preservation or revision.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Classification and request history help orient impact inquiry but do not replace dependency evidence.

Comprehension assumptions

Decision authority and domain meaning must be established; disputed intent cannot be resolved by test count. The requester and maintainer must share enough domain meaning to distinguish a fault from a newly desired behaviour.

Oracle and regression limits

Acceptance examples can misunderstand the request; separately inspect preserved obligations.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

A purpose label says nothing by itself about API or schema compatibility; determine these where an intervention reaches them.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

Classification is informational; any subsequent intervention must separately justify code, state and external-effect recovery.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Requesting/accepting stakeholders, maintainers and affected consumers need a shared account of what is and is not promised.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

A short accepted issue with concrete examples is enough for a bounded low-risk change; reject or defer an unjustified request. Reject, defer or retire work without a justified benefit or surviving obligation; abandon redundant classification paperwork.

    Judgement
    Protected mechanism

    State the requested behavioural difference, surviving obligations and decision authority; challenge ambiguous or conflicting requests before treating tests as acceptance.

    Minimal adequate alternative

    Use an existing unambiguous authorised request; no new board or document is needed. Decline changes without a supported objective.

    Fuller form trigger

    New, disputed or externally imposed change objectives, including urgent corrections.

    Cost of simplification

    An informal exchange can leave competing interpretations or missing participants undiscoverable later; retain an explicit decision when that uncertainty matters.

    Retirement condition

    Compare change with continued useful operation and retirement. End a classification or approval artefact when no consumer uses its distinction, while preserving any actual authorisation requirement.

    Approval can institutionalise an obsolete requirement, exclude affected users or become a bottleneck; procedural approval is not evidence that the goal is beneficial.

    Cheap or nontrigger

    Use an existing unambiguous authorised request; no new board or document is needed. Decline changes without a supported objective.

Omission retirement conditions:

Canonical

Omit a mechanism when its trigger is absent or a cheaper adequate substitute establishes the actual obligation; retire it when its protected obligation or consumer ends. Do not use omission to waive an unchanged supported outcome.

Omit or retire a control when its protected obligation, relevant failure mechanism or decision consumer no longer exists; record unresolved support consequences before removing it.

Neutral later crosswalk questions:

Same object: legitimate intended difference and preserved/revised obligations. Both deny that tests or a proposal create authority. Retain the criterion, not a particular approval ritual.

Problem addressed:

Avoid category-induced blind spots and misleading maintenance proportions.

Failure mode:

A classification label is treated as the whole maintenance task and hides mixed purposes or required work.

Mechanism:

Use purpose labels alongside observable activity and artefact scope, permitting multiple purposes; include additive and emergency distinctions when using the 2022 terminology.

Trigger context:

Classification affects estimates, authorisation, reporting or selection of maintenance evidence.

Non trigger cheap path:

Do not label every commit when the label changes no decision; one explanatory sentence may suffice.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • The taxonomy edition, unit and use must be declared.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C001

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

Classification affects estimates, authorisation, reporting or selection of maintenance evidence. Identify whose intended result is changing and distinguish corrective, adaptive, perfective, preventive, additive and emergency dimensions without forcing exclusivity.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Request intent and actual changed artefacts. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.

Preservation obligation and observer

Request owner for intention; analyst for observed activities. A request owner or affected stakeholder supplies legitimate intent; observation of existing behaviour alone cannot authorise its preservation or revision.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Classification and request history help orient impact inquiry but do not replace dependency evidence.

Comprehension assumptions

The taxonomy edition, unit and use must be declared. The requester and maintainer must share enough domain meaning to distinguish a fault from a newly desired behaviour.

Oracle and regression limits

Acceptance examples can misunderstand the request; separately inspect preserved obligations.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

A purpose label says nothing by itself about API or schema compatibility; determine these where an intervention reaches them.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

Classification is informational; any subsequent intervention must separately justify code, state and external-effect recovery.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Requesting/accepting stakeholders, maintainers and affected consumers need a shared account of what is and is not promised.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

Do not label every commit when the label changes no decision; one explanatory sentence may suffice. Reject, defer or retire work without a justified benefit or surviving obligation; abandon redundant classification paperwork.

Domain variant policy:

The input-scoped variants below supplement the canonical formulation only under their own triggers; they are alternatives/facets, not a universal conjunction of all controls.

Expected payoff:

Hypothesis

Avoid category-induced blind spots and misleading maintenance proportions.

Qualification

A conditional engineering rationale, not a universal quantified or experimentally certified payoff.

Request owner for intention; analyst for observed activities.

Original form:

  • Input property key

    A:ESME-003

    Form

    Maintenance guidance includes preparation and modification of more than delivered source code.

Problem addressed:

Prevent changes that are source-correct but unbuildable, unoperable or unmaintainable.

Failure mode:

A consequential non-code dependency is omitted, leaving source changes insufficient for the actual maintenance obligation.

Mechanism:

Include build, configuration, data, documentation and other non-code objects only where a current or planned maintenance obligation depends on them.

Trigger context:

A maintenance task depends on consequential state outside conventional source code.

Non trigger cheap path:

Keep the scope local; no organisation-wide inventory is required when the relevant inputs and consumers are already known.

Dependencies preconditions:

A concrete maintenance obligation and enough impact evidence to identify consequential non-code artefacts; no general inventory requirement.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

A future or current maintenance task depends on non-code state or transfer readiness. Identify whose intended result is changing and distinguish corrective, adaptive, perfective, preventive, additive and emergency dimensions without forcing exclusivity.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Code, build inputs, schemas, configurations, operational instructions and handover material. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.

Preservation obligation and observer

Maintainer, operator and downstream consumer of the actual artefact. A request owner or affected stakeholder supplies legitimate intent; observation of existing behaviour alone cannot authorise its preservation or revision.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Classification and request history help orient impact inquiry but do not replace dependency evidence.

Comprehension assumptions

Artefact relevance must be tied to a concrete maintenance obligation. The requester and maintainer must share enough domain meaning to distinguish a fault from a newly desired behaviour.

Oracle and regression limits

Acceptance examples can misunderstand the request; separately inspect preserved obligations.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

A purpose label says nothing by itself about API or schema compatibility; determine these where an intervention reaches them.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

Classification is informational; any subsequent intervention must separately justify code, state and external-effect recovery.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Requesting/accepting stakeholders, maintainers and affected consumers need a shared account of what is and is not promised.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

Exclude irrelevant artefacts explicitly rather than constructing an organisation-wide inventory for a local task. Reject, defer or retire work without a justified benefit or surviving obligation; abandon redundant classification paperwork.

Domain variant policy:

The input-scoped variants below supplement the canonical formulation only under their own triggers; they are alternatives/facets, not a universal conjunction of all controls.

Expected payoff:

Hypothesis

Prevent changes that are source-correct but unbuildable, unoperable or unmaintainable.

Qualification

A conditional engineering rationale, not a universal quantified or experimentally certified payoff.

Decision consumer:

Consumer

Maintainer, operator and downstream consumer of the actual artefact.

Decision

Necessary non-code changes and readiness dependencies are included in scope and assigned a consumer.

Subject bearer:

Consequential code and non-code artefacts within a stated maintenance obligation.

Criterion:

The consequential non-code objects and their consumers are in the scope, with irrelevant objects omitted explicitly when disputed.

Operating mechanism:

Include build, configuration, data, documentation and other non-code objects only where a current or planned maintenance obligation depends on them.

Required inputs:

A concrete maintenance obligation and enough impact evidence to identify consequential non-code artefacts; no general inventory requirement.

Outputs evidence constraints:

The consequential non-code objects and their consumers are in the scope, with irrelevant objects omitted explicitly when disputed.

Actor authority boundary:

Actors

Maintainer, operator and downstream consumer of the actual artefact.

Boundary

Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

Communication interaction requirement:

Exchange

Code, build inputs, schemas, configurations, operational instructions and handover material.

Purpose

Enable the stated consumer to judge the mechanism, assumptions and postcondition. Use the cheapest adequate channel in NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH; mere publication is not successful communication.

Observable postcondition:

The consequential non-code objects and their consumers are in the scope, with irrelevant objects omitted explicitly when disputed.

    Form

Problem addressed:

Transferred artefacts may not enable a new maintainer to diagnose or change the system.

Failure mode:

Artefacts are handed over without a capable willing recipient able to perform supported work.

Mechanism:

At a transfer or continuity risk, establish that an actual willing recipient has the knowledge, access, time and practical ability to perform representative supported work; use explanation, supervised work or equivalent evidence.

Trigger context:

Initial handover, onboarding, departure, concentration or a new support obligation threatens practical maintenance capability.

Non trigger cheap path:

One representative diagnosis or change can suffice; stable small projects may instead make support limits or retirement explicit, without inventing extra maintainers.

Dependencies preconditions:

A real willing recipient, relevant knowledge and artefacts, practical access, time and an opportunity to demonstrate representative supported work. Initial delivery and later turnover are different triggers of the same capability criterion.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

Ownership transfer, new maintainer onboarding or impending loss of specialised knowledge. Change may concern code, ownership, support, dependency substitution or ending operation. No-change is legitimate when obligations remain met.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Include artefacts, access, build/dependency identity, human knowledge, support promises and consumer relationships relevant to continuity.

Preservation obligation and observer

The receiver can complete a representative task or the handoff plan changes to address demonstrated gaps. Preserve accepted service/data/support obligations during handoff or retirement, not indefinite operation or every historical implementation detail.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Declared dependency networks identify possible exposure; actual use, transitive obligations and human responsibility require additional evidence.

Comprehension assumptions

A willing receiving maintainer, operational access and time to learn; a quiz alone is not enough. Demonstrate bounded maintenance ability through tasks and dialogue. Commit history, popularity and documents remain incomplete expertise proxies.

Oracle and regression limits

A successful rehearsal does not prove broad competence; task selection can conceal rare but important failure modes. A successful onboarding task or archived build is partial evidence, not proof of readiness for every failure. Inactivity needs interpretation rather than automatic failure classification.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

Deprecation needs a feasible transition or explicit exception; forks and replacements transfer maintenance obligations rather than eliminating them.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

Shutdown, dependency replacement and ownership transfer need contingency conditions appropriate to actual data/service effects; archival retention alone cannot restore a service.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Delivering and receiving maintainers exchange knowledge; managers provide time and authority rather than infer competence from attendance.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

Pair on one meaningful change or diagnosis instead of producing a comprehensive handover manual. Fund sustainable capacity or choose a feasible alternative. Retire operational systems and artefacts when their justified consumers/obligations end, preserving only required historical custody.

Domain variant policy:

The input-scoped variants below supplement the canonical formulation only under their own triggers; they are alternatives/facets, not a universal conjunction of all controls.

Expected payoff:

Hypothesis

Transfer actionable expertise and expose missing environmental knowledge.

Qualification

Conditional payoff, not a guarantee or a measured effect unless explicitly established by an individual empirical source.

Decision consumer:

Delivering and receiving maintainers exchange knowledge; managers provide time and authority rather than infer competence from attendance.

Subject bearer:

The actual recipient or continuing maintenance group and its supported work.

Criterion:

The recipient can perform the relevant supported work, or the remaining capability/support limitation is explicit and acted upon.

Operating mechanism:

At a transfer or continuity risk, establish that an actual willing recipient has the knowledge, access, time and practical ability to perform representative supported work; use explanation, supervised work or equivalent evidence.

Required inputs:

A real willing recipient, relevant knowledge and artefacts, practical access, time and an opportunity to demonstrate representative supported work. Initial delivery and later turnover are different triggers of the same capability criterion.

Outputs evidence constraints:

The recipient can perform the relevant supported work, or the remaining capability/support limitation is explicit and acted upon.

Actor authority boundary:

Delivering and receiving maintainers exchange knowledge; managers provide time and authority rather than infer competence from attendance.

Communication interaction requirement:

Recipient and boundary

Delivering and receiving maintainers exchange knowledge; managers provide time and authority rather than infer competence from attendance.

Content

Use representative tasks, access checks and dialogue to test the receiving maintainer’s ability; preserve rationale and unresolved questions that the task exposes.

Adequacy test

The receiver can complete a representative task or the handoff plan changes to address demonstrated gaps.

Non requirement

No separate person, meeting, registry or tool is required merely because the analytical roles are distinct.

Observable postcondition:

The recipient can perform the relevant supported work, or the remaining capability/support limitation is explicit and acted upon.

    • Knowledge cannot be reduced to a repository database, and an owner label does not create willingness or capacity. Hidden consumers and indefinite obligations can prevent simple retirement.

Evolved form:

At a transfer or continuity risk, establish that an actual willing recipient has the knowledge, access, time and practical ability to perform representative supported work; use explanation, supervised work or equivalent evidence. Outcome: The recipient can perform the relevant supported work, or the remaining capability/support limitation is explicit and acted upon.

Ceremony property judgement:

Canonical

A declared analytical criterion is not automatically a required artefact, role, test stack or meeting. Use the trigger and cheaper adequate realisation; adverse/unresolved rows are not implementation instructions.

Input judgements
  • Input property key

    A:ESME-003

    Judgement
    Essential

    Necessary non-code changes and readiness dependencies are included in scope and assigned a consumer.

    Minimal alternative

    Exclude irrelevant artefacts explicitly rather than constructing an organisation-wide inventory for a local task.

    Anti ceremony

    Presence of an artefact, tool name, meeting or metric does not establish the postcondition; remove it when its protected failure and consumer disappear.

  • Input property key

    A:ESME-064

    Judgement
    Essential

    A successor can carry out representative supported work or the remaining limitation is explicit.

    Minimal alternative

    A small stable project may need a clear support/retirement policy rather than recruiting multiple maintainers.

    Anti ceremony

    Presence of an artefact, tool name, meeting or metric does not establish the postcondition; remove it when its protected failure and consumer disappear.

  • Input property key

    B:ESME-004

    Judgement
    Protected mechanism

    Before transferring responsibility, establish the receiving maintainer’s access, runnable artefacts, known obligations and escalation route; revisit after ownership changes.

    Minimal adequate alternative

    An existing competent team with unchanged access can reuse its arrangements; no separate transition ceremony is inherently required.

    Fuller form trigger

    Initial delivery, outsourcing, major platform change or ownership handoff.

    Cost of simplification

    An informal handover may fail to expose missing credentials, unavailable expertise or unusable artefacts; a small capability check can reveal these failures.

    Retirement condition

    Compare change with continued useful operation and retirement. End a classification or approval artefact when no consumer uses its distinction, while preserving any actual authorisation requirement.

    Ledger id

    ESME-CS004

    Possible artefact or ritual

    Formal transfer checklist and handover meeting

  • Input property key

    B:ESME-056

    Judgement
    Protected mechanism

    Use representative tasks, access checks and dialogue to test the receiving maintainer’s ability; preserve rationale and unresolved questions that the task exposes.

    Minimal adequate alternative

    Pair on one meaningful change or diagnosis instead of producing a comprehensive handover manual.

    Fuller form trigger

    Ownership transfer, new maintainer onboarding or impending loss of specialised knowledge.

    Cost of simplification

    A small practical task samples only part of capability; broaden demonstrations when the new responsibility spans materially different operations.

    Retirement condition

    Fund sustainable capacity or choose a feasible alternative. Retire operational systems and artefacts when their justified consumers/obligations end, preserving only required historical custody.

    Ledger id

    ESME-CS056

    Possible artefact or ritual

    Handover attendance or documentation-completion certificate

Canonical disposition:

RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

Disposition rationale:

A-003 readiness, A-064 succession and B-004/B-056 describe the same recipient-capability invariant at different times. Merge initial transfer and later succession as guarded applications; keep willingness, access, time and representative-task evidence. A roster or delivery bundle is not the postcondition.

Conditionally crosswalk worthy:

true

Historical provenance

Source traditions have scoped ancestry; this operative canonical wording is an analytical adjudication, not a historical quotation.

Theoretical support

No new formal theorem is claimed. Apply inherited formal results only within their recorded model and access scope.

Comparative empirical support

Setting-, question- and outcome-specific; citations are not pooled as a common effect estimate.

Field support

A published case or deployment account does not establish a representative rate or whole-system payoff.

Replication

Two frozen analytical executions are not independent empirical replications of their shared underlying studies.

Reconciliation confidence

Explicit semantic mapping with preserved counterpositions; confidence is qualitative, not a calibrated probability.

Transferability

Conditional on the actual trigger, observer, authority, capability and cost; no target adoption is decided.

Reconciliation access boundary

The frozen records and their claim/access accounts were inspected here. The underlying articles, PDFs and web pages were not re-accessed in this reconciliation; their original access is inherited, not independently certified. Custody and internal consistency do not establish scholarly truth.

Neutral later crosswalk questions:

  • Does this subject have the stated trigger: Initial handover, onboarding, departure, concentration or a new support obligation threatens practical maintenance capability.

  • What evidence establishes or defeats the scoped criterion: The recipient can perform the relevant supported work, or the remaining capability/support limitation is explicit and acted upon.

  • Would the cheaper/non-trigger path suffice: One representative diagnosis or change can suffice; stable small projects may instead make support limits or retirement explicit, without inventing extra maintainers.

  • Who actually consumes the result and has legitimate capable authority to act; is non-change, repair, restructuring, migration, restricted servicing or retirement the justified outcome?

A-003 readiness, A-064 succession and B-004/B-056 describe the same recipient-capability invariant at different times. Merge initial transfer and later succession as guarded applications; keep willingness, access, time and representative-task evidence. A roster or delivery bundle is not the postcondition.

Problem addressed:

Reduce wrong-baseline diagnosis and unverifiable change attribution.

Failure mode:

Analysis, evidence or release action refers to the wrong or unreconstructible baseline and environment.

Mechanism:

Identify and retain the exact baseline and configuration needed to interpret, build, compare or restore the changed system.

Trigger context:

An intervention or investigation requires attributing differences or returning to a known state.

Non trigger cheap path:

A versioned file and recorded command can suffice for a local deterministic artefact; retain richer dependencies only where needed.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • Referenced artefacts remain accessible and configuration identifiers resolve.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C046

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

An intervention or investigation requires attributing differences or returning to a known state. Identify whose intended result is changing and distinguish corrective, adaptive, perfective, preventive, additive and emergency dimensions without forcing exclusivity.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Source revision, build inputs, package versions, configuration and relevant data-state reference. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.

Preservation obligation and observer

Reviewer and operator comparing the same system, not merely matching a branch name. A request owner or affected stakeholder supplies legitimate intent; observation of existing behaviour alone cannot authorise its preservation or revision.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Classification and request history help orient impact inquiry but do not replace dependency evidence.

Comprehension assumptions

Referenced artefacts remain accessible and configuration identifiers resolve. The requester and maintainer must share enough domain meaning to distinguish a fault from a newly desired behaviour.

Oracle and regression limits

Acceptance examples can misunderstand the request; separately inspect preserved obligations.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

A purpose label says nothing by itself about API or schema compatibility; determine these where an intervention reaches them.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

Classification is informational; any subsequent intervention must separately justify code, state and external-effect recovery.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Requesting/accepting stakeholders, maintainers and affected consumers need a shared account of what is and is not promised.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

A versioned file and recorded command can suffice for a local deterministic artefact; retain richer dependencies only where needed. Reject, defer or retire work without a justified benefit or surviving obligation; abandon redundant classification paperwork.

Domain variant policy:

The input-scoped variants below supplement the canonical formulation only under their own triggers; they are alternatives/facets, not a universal conjunction of all controls.

Expected payoff:

Hypothesis

Reduce wrong-baseline diagnosis and unverifiable change attribution.

Qualification

A conditional engineering rationale, not a universal quantified or experimentally certified payoff.

    Judgement
    Protected mechanism

    Bind change and evidence to recoverable versions of the relevant source, configuration, build inputs and data/schema state; distinguish identity from recoverability.

    Minimal adequate alternative

    Use existing versioned inputs and reproducible commands; do not snapshot irrelevant infrastructure or duplicate authoritative history.

    Cost of simplification

    A lighter baseline may omit a mutable build input, schema or remote state; include any omitted input capable of changing the relevant result.

    Retirement condition

    Compare change with continued useful operation and retirement. End a classification or approval artefact when no consumer uses its distinction, while preserving any actual authorisation requirement.

Mechanism:

Authorise a bounded temporary change of objective, including disabling or degrading capability when that contains a more consequential failure; state residual obligations, accepted loss, observation and follow-up.

Trigger context:

An incident or serious exposure makes ordinary repair timing unsafe and a feasible containment action can reduce harm.

Non trigger cheap path:

Use normal repair or deliberate non-change when urgency is absent; a simple reversible feature disablement can need only proportionate evidence.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • Containment scope, operational capability and recovery or follow-up must be credible.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C001

  • ESME-C049

  • ESME-C006

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

Continuing the current fault causes greater immediate harm than a controlled degraded state. Identify whose intended result is changing and distinguish corrective, adaptive, perfective, preventive, additive and emergency dimensions without forcing exclusivity.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Live service, temporary configuration or patch and follow-up obligation. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.

Preservation obligation and observer

Affected users and the person authorised to accept temporary degradation. A request owner or affected stakeholder supplies legitimate intent; observation of existing behaviour alone cannot authorise its preservation or revision.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Classification and request history help orient impact inquiry but do not replace dependency evidence.

Comprehension assumptions

Containment scope, operational capability and recovery or follow-up must be credible. The requester and maintainer must share enough domain meaning to distinguish a fault from a newly desired behaviour.

Oracle and regression limits

Acceptance examples can misunderstand the request; separately inspect preserved obligations.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

A purpose label says nothing by itself about API or schema compatibility; determine these where an intervention reaches them.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

Classification is informational; any subsequent intervention must separately justify code, state and external-effect recovery.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Requesting/accepting stakeholders, maintainers and affected consumers need a shared account of what is and is not promised.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

Use normal repair when delay is tolerable; do not invent an emergency fast lane for ordinary convenience. Reject, defer or retire work without a justified benefit or surviving obligation; abandon redundant classification paperwork.

Domain variant policy:

The input-scoped variants below supplement the canonical formulation only under their own triggers; they are alternatives/facets, not a universal conjunction of all controls.

Expected payoff:

Hypothesis

Limit immediate loss without silently redefining the long-term service.

Qualification

A conditional engineering rationale, not a universal quantified or experimentally certified payoff.

Decision consumer:

Consumer

Affected users and the person authorised to accept temporary degradation.

Decision

Temporary degradation and its accepted scope are visible, with a named follow-up decision rather than presumed final correctness.

Subject bearer:

Live service, temporary configuration or patch and follow-up obligation. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.

Criterion:

The accepted containment objective is achieved within its loss and authority boundary, with recovery or permanent resolution still owned.

Operating mechanism:

Authorise a bounded temporary change of objective, including disabling or degrading capability when that contains a more consequential failure; state residual obligations, accepted loss, observation and follow-up.

Candidate proposes requiring every maintenance activity to fit exactly one of four boxes.

An audit or metric system attempts to treat four labels as exhaustive and exclusive.

The analyst using the categories to make comparisons. A request owner or affected stakeholder supplies legitimate intent; observation of existing behaviour alone cannot authorise its preservation or revision.

Classification is informational; any subsequent intervention must separately justify code, state and external-effect recovery.

Original form:

  • Input property key

    A:ESME-007

    Form

    Evolution research explains software embedded in a changing human and technical environment through feedback.

  • Input property key

    B:ESME-006

    Form

    Lehman’s evolution programme treats usage, adaptation, effort, familiarity and organisation as a feedback system.

Problem addressed:

Detect genuine adaptation needs without mandating expansion.

Failure mode:

Environment and use change while the maintenance decision continues to assume the old conditions.

Mechanism:

Observe changes in use, expectations and constraints; decide whether adaptation, servicing, unchanged operation or retirement best preserves justified usefulness.

Trigger context:

Evidence of changed environment, user dissatisfaction or new constraints, not age alone.

Non trigger cheap path:

For a stable environment, use occasional review or existing user feedback rather than continuous change.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • Environmental observations must be relevant and not just proxy growth metrics.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C001

  • ESME-C081

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

Evidence of changed environment, user dissatisfaction or new constraints, not age alone. Study environmental fit, complexity, familiarity and change rate; do not infer a mandate to grow from an observed growth curve.

Baseline and affected artefacts

System-environment relationship and observed user outcomes. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.

Preservation obligation and observer

Users and stakeholders whose activity the software serves. Usefulness belongs to actual users and environments; LOC, release size and observed effort are different observables.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Feedback crosses users, organisation and technical structure; correlation alone does not identify a causal channel.

Comprehension assumptions

Environmental observations must be relevant and not just proxy growth metrics. Maintainers must understand what a metric counts and which environmental assumptions remained stable.

Oracle and regression limits

Historical fit does not validate future predictions; a counterexample may concern sampling rather than the whole theory.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

A historical trend does not establish a compatibility constraint; such obligations require separate consumer evidence.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

The explanatory model does not deploy code: operational rollback is not applicable until a concrete intervention is chosen.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Analysts explain conditional trends to those deciding staffing, investment, evolution, servicing or closure.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

For a stable environment, use occasional review or existing user feedback rather than continuous change. Retain a useful unchanged system where obligations permit; retire a metric or model when its measurement assumptions no longer hold.

Domain variant policy:

The input-scoped variants below supplement the canonical formulation only under their own triggers; they are alternatives/facets, not a universal conjunction of all controls.

Expected payoff:

Hypothesis

Detect genuine adaptation needs without mandating expansion.

Qualification

A conditional engineering rationale, not a universal quantified or experimentally certified payoff.

Decision consumer:

Consumer

Users and stakeholders whose activity the software serves.

Decision

An identified change in environmental fit has a reasoned response, which may be no change.

Subject bearer:

System-environment relationship and observed user outcomes. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.

Criterion:

An identified change in environmental fit has a reasoned response, which may be no change.

Operating mechanism:

Observe changes in use, expectations and constraints; decide whether adaptation, servicing, unchanged operation or retirement best preserves justified usefulness.

Required inputs:

Conditions

  • Environmental observations must be relevant and not just proxy growth metrics.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C001

  • ESME-C081

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Outputs evidence constraints:

An identified change in environmental fit has a reasoned response, which may be no change.

Actor authority boundary:

Actors

Users and stakeholders whose activity the software serves.

Boundary

Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

Communication interaction requirement:

Exchange

System-environment relationship and observed user outcomes.

Purpose

Enable the stated consumer to judge the mechanism, assumptions and postcondition. Use the cheapest adequate channel in NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH; mere publication is not successful communication.

Observable postcondition:

An identified change in environmental fit has a reasoned response, which may be no change.

Input judgements
  • Input property key

    A:ESME-007

    Judgement
    Essential

    An identified change in environmental fit has a reasoned response, which may be no change.

    Minimal alternative

    For a stable environment, use occasional review or existing user feedback rather than continuous change.

    Anti ceremony

    Presence of an artefact, tool name, meeting or metric does not establish the postcondition; remove it when its protected failure and consumer disappear.

  • Input property key

    B:ESME-006

    Judgement
    Protected mechanism

    Observe demand, delivered effects, effort and consequences over time; revise change priorities when those observations challenge the operative model.

    Minimal adequate alternative

    For infrequent bounded changes, a direct outcome review may suffice; do not institute a metric programme without a decision consumer.

    Fuller form trigger

    Repeated change in a system exposed to evolving use and stakeholder expectations.

    Cost of simplification

    Direct occasional review can miss slow trends and cross-team effects; use time-series observation when those effects change real decisions.

    Retirement condition

    Observe at a scale where results can change decisions; retire unused dashboards or metrics. Include measurement cost and the option of a stable useful system.

    Ledger id

    ESME-CS006

    Possible artefact or ritual

    Evolution dashboard and regular review meeting

Disposition rationale:

Shared feedback view: usefulness changes with environment and demand, not only with code edits. Preserve the ability to revise a proposal or choose no change instead of translating evolution into endless growth.

Problem addressed:

Failure mode:

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

Someone invokes an evolution law without identifying system class, measure or environment. Study environmental fit, complexity, familiarity and change rate; do not infer a mandate to grow from an observed growth curve.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Release histories and environmental conditions. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.

Preservation obligation and observer

Actual users, not an age or LOC threshold. Usefulness belongs to actual users and environments; LOC, release size and observed effort are different observables.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Feedback crosses users, organisation and technical structure; correlation alone does not identify a causal channel.

Comprehension assumptions

Universal inevitability is not established by the studied populations. Maintainers must understand what a metric counts and which environmental assumptions remained stable.

Oracle and regression limits

Historical fit does not validate future predictions; a counterexample may concern sampling rather than the whole theory.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

A historical trend does not establish a compatibility constraint; such obligations require separate consumer evidence.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

The explanatory model does not deploy code: operational rollback is not applicable until a concrete intervention is chosen.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Analysts explain conditional trends to those deciding staffing, investment, evolution, servicing or closure.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

Assess actual usefulness and obligations through ESME-C008 instead. Retain a useful unchanged system where obligations permit; retire a metric or model when its measurement assumptions no longer hold.

Problem addressed:

Prevent a measurement artefact from becoming a universal maintenance rule.

Failure mode:

Different populations, metrics or programme categories are treated as interchangeable evidence for an evolution claim.

Mechanism:

Before using an evolution regularity, state its population, measure, time horizon, model and empirical exceptions; narrow or withhold the forecast when these change.

Trigger context:

Growth, complexity, effort or decline measurements guide investment or generalisation.

Non trigger cheap path:

Use a simple trend with explicit units when it directly answers the decision; no statistical model is mandatory.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • Consistent measurement and a declared transfer population.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C008

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

Growth, complexity, effort or decline measurements guide investment or generalisation. Study environmental fit, complexity, familiarity and change rate; do not infer a mandate to grow from an observed growth curve.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Release sample, size/function/effort measures and data-extraction rules. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.

Preservation obligation and observer

Analyst and decision maker interpreting the metric. Usefulness belongs to actual users and environments; LOC, release size and observed effort are different observables.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Feedback crosses users, organisation and technical structure; correlation alone does not identify a causal channel.

Comprehension assumptions

Consistent measurement and a declared transfer population. Maintainers must understand what a metric counts and which environmental assumptions remained stable.

Oracle and regression limits

Historical fit does not validate future predictions; a counterexample may concern sampling rather than the whole theory.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

A historical trend does not establish a compatibility constraint; such obligations require separate consumer evidence.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

The explanatory model does not deploy code: operational rollback is not applicable until a concrete intervention is chosen.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Analysts explain conditional trends to those deciding staffing, investment, evolution, servicing or closure.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

Use a simple trend with explicit units when it directly answers the decision; no statistical model is mandatory. Retain a useful unchanged system where obligations permit; retire a metric or model when its measurement assumptions no longer hold.

Domain variant policy:

The input-scoped variants below supplement the canonical formulation only under their own triggers; they are alternatives/facets, not a universal conjunction of all controls.

Expected payoff:

Hypothesis

Prevent a measurement artefact from becoming a universal maintenance rule.

Qualification

A conditional engineering rationale, not a universal quantified or experimentally certified payoff.

Decision consumer:

Consumer

Analyst and decision maker interpreting the metric.

Decision

The claim states its population and measure, and contrary samples remain visible.

Subject bearer:

Release sample, size/function/effort measures and data-extraction rules. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.

Criterion:

The claim and its planning use have a declared domain and contrary evidence rather than an unqualified law.

Problem addressed:

Avoid change throughput that destroys ability to maintain or recover the system.

Failure mode:

A change programme exceeds the knowledge and capability available to sustain it.

Mechanism:

Use observed comprehension, review and recovery demand to constrain change intake and invest in knowledge when understanding becomes a bottleneck.

Trigger context:

Change volume or personnel turnover outpaces demonstrated ability to understand and maintain obligations.

Non trigger cheap path:

A small expert-maintained component may need only a direct conversation and modest change cadence.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • Workload signals must distinguish familiarity from tooling, task complexity and organisational restrictions.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C013

  • ESME-C004

  • ESME-C072

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

Change volume or personnel turnover outpaces demonstrated ability to understand and maintain obligations. Study environmental fit, complexity, familiarity and change rate; do not infer a mandate to grow from an observed growth curve.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Maintainer knowledge, workload, change volume and review outcomes. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.

Preservation obligation and observer

Maintainers and those allocating time, not a fixed universal staffing formula. Usefulness belongs to actual users and environments; LOC, release size and observed effort are different observables.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Feedback crosses users, organisation and technical structure; correlation alone does not identify a causal channel.

Comprehension assumptions

Workload signals must distinguish familiarity from tooling, task complexity and organisational restrictions. Maintainers must understand what a metric counts and which environmental assumptions remained stable.

Oracle and regression limits

Historical fit does not validate future predictions; a counterexample may concern sampling rather than the whole theory.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

A historical trend does not establish a compatibility constraint; such obligations require separate consumer evidence.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

The explanatory model does not deploy code: operational rollback is not applicable until a concrete intervention is chosen.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Analysts explain conditional trends to those deciding staffing, investment, evolution, servicing or closure.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

A small expert-maintained component may need only a direct conversation and modest change cadence. Retain a useful unchanged system where obligations permit; retire a metric or model when its measurement assumptions no longer hold.

Omission retirement conditions:

Canonical

Omit a mechanism when its trigger is absent or a cheaper adequate substitute establishes the actual obligation; retire it when its protected obligation or consumer ends. Do not use omission to waive an unchanged supported outcome.

Input specific
  • Input property key

    A:ESME-011

    Conditions

    Measure local capacity and uncertainty using ESME-C011. Omit or retire a control when its protected obligation, relevant failure mechanism or decision consumer no longer exists; record unresolved support consequences before removing it.

Neutral later crosswalk questions:

  • Does this subject have the stated trigger: A plan invokes a universal rate to dismiss changed capability or demand.

  • What evidence establishes or defeats the scoped criterion: Forecasts retain uncertainty and do not treat changed conditions as impossible by definition.

  • Would the cheaper/non-trigger path suffice: Measure local capacity and uncertainty using ESME-C011.

  • Who actually consumes the result and has legitimate capable authority to act; is non-change, repair, restructuring, migration, restricted servicing or retirement the justified outcome?

A explicitly examined a separate invariant-work-rate planning claim. Reject that guarantee, not the usefulness of observing actual capacity.

Problem addressed:

Avoid both blind editing and unbounded analysis that consumes the maintenance budget.

Failure mode:

The maintainer acts without the task-relevant understanding needed for the consequential decision.

Mechanism:

Establish enough understanding to discriminate the pending change decision; expand inquiry when observed contradictions or impact escape invalidate that boundary.

Trigger context:

A maintainer cannot explain the relevant effect or uncertainty of a proposed intervention.

Non trigger cheap path:

Inspect the relevant code, test and domain example directly for a small familiar change; avoid mandatory reconstruction of everything.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • The pending decision and consequential unknowns must be stated.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C001

  • ESME-C022

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

A maintainer cannot explain the relevant effect or uncertainty of a proposed intervention. Select the question needed for a proposed change, diagnosis or handover rather than presupposing whole-system understanding.

Baseline and affected artefacts

The affected feature and evidence needed for the current decision. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

Preservation obligation and observer

Maintainer and reviewer who must act, with domain experts where intent is lost. Distinguish a recovered description from an authorised requirement and from what an actual user can observe.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Static relations overapproximate modelled paths; dynamic traces underapproximate possible executions; fuse only with declared boundaries.

Comprehension assumptions

The pending decision and consequential unknowns must be stated. Incomplete intent, unsupported languages, generated code and tacit operational knowledge limit recovery.

Oracle and regression limits

Recovered models require cross-checking; observed behaviour can be a defect and absent evidence is not evidence of absence.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

Recovery may reveal interface or migration assumptions but cannot itself establish their validity.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

Read-only inquiry normally needs no production rollback; intrusive instrumentation must control perturbation and cleanup.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Maintainers and domain/operational experts exchange concrete questions and evidence; documentation is useful through an actual consumer.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

Inspect the relevant code, test and domain example directly for a small familiar change; avoid mandatory reconstruction of everything. Stop inquiry when it discriminates the pending decision sufficiently; deepen it when contradictions or impact escape appear; retire stale views.

Domain variant policy:

The input-scoped variants below supplement the canonical formulation only under their own triggers; they are alternatives/facets, not a universal conjunction of all controls.

Hypothesis

Avoid both blind editing and unbounded analysis that consumes the maintenance budget.

Ceremony property judgement:

Canonical

A declared analytical criterion is not automatically a required artefact, role, test stack or meeting. Use the trigger and cheaper adequate realisation; adverse/unresolved rows are not implementation instructions.

Input judgements
  • Input property key

    A:ESME-012

    Judgement
    Essential

    The maintainer can answer the consequential change questions and state remaining uncertainty.

    Minimal alternative

    Inspect the relevant code, test and domain example directly for a small familiar change; avoid mandatory reconstruction of everything.

    Anti ceremony

    Presence of an artefact, tool name, meeting or metric does not establish the postcondition; remove it when its protected failure and consumer disappear.

  • Input property key

    B:ESME-011

    Judgement
    Protected mechanism

    Identify the questions needed for this change, seek evidence until consequential uncertainties are bounded, and expand inquiry when evidence contradicts the model.

    Minimal adequate alternative

    Reuse reliable knowledge and perform a small confirming check when the question is local and low consequence.

    Fuller form trigger

    A change depends on unfamiliar behaviour, ownership, dependencies or intent.

    Cost of simplification

    Bounded inquiry can miss a question that would change the intervention; retain an explicit trigger for expanding inquiry when observations disagree.

    Retirement condition

    Stop inquiry when the consequential question is adequately supported at acceptable risk; expand on contrary evidence. Retain only explanations with plausible future consumers.

Problem addressed:

Reduce irrelevant code considered without claiming a complete specification.

Failure mode:

A dependence model omits relevant effects or its conservative result is mistaken for precise complete behavioural understanding.

Mechanism:

Use a declared slicing criterion and static dependence model to find potentially relevant statements, with explicit language, alias and environment assumptions.

Trigger context:

A consequential comprehension or impact question benefits from model-based relevance beyond a single observed run.

Non trigger cheap path:

Direct inspection suffices for a small obvious dependence; no slicing tool is required.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • Sound dependencies and supported semantics; minimal arbitrary slices are not computable in general.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C013

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

A data/control relevance question can be expressed in the supported program model. Select the question needed for a proposed change, diagnosis or handover rather than presupposing whole-system understanding.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Program statements, variable criterion and control/data dependencies. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

Preservation obligation and observer

The observation specified by the slicing criterion, not every external effect. Distinguish a recovered description from an authorised requirement and from what an actual user can observe.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Static relations overapproximate modelled paths; dynamic traces underapproximate possible executions; fuse only with declared boundaries.

Comprehension assumptions

Sound dependencies and supported semantics; minimal arbitrary slices are not computable in general. Incomplete intent, unsupported languages, generated code and tacit operational knowledge limit recovery.

Oracle and regression limits

Recovered models require cross-checking; observed behaviour can be a defect and absent evidence is not evidence of absence.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

Recovery may reveal interface or migration assumptions but cannot itself establish their validity.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

Read-only inquiry normally needs no production rollback; intrusive instrumentation must control perturbation and cleanup.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Maintainers and domain/operational experts exchange concrete questions and evidence; documentation is useful through an actual consumer.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

Manual inspection or a small dependency query may dominate building a slicer. Stop inquiry when it discriminates the pending decision sufficiently; deepen it when contradictions or impact escape appear; retire stale views.

Domain variant policy:

The input-scoped variants below supplement the canonical formulation only under their own triggers; they are alternatives/facets, not a universal conjunction of all controls.

Hypothesis

Reduce irrelevant code considered without claiming a complete specification.

A conditional engineering rationale, not a universal quantified or experimentally certified payoff.

The observation specified by the slicing criterion, not every external effect.

Program statements, variable criterion and control/data dependencies. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

Operating mechanism:

Use a declared slicing criterion and static dependence model to find potentially relevant statements, with explicit language, alias and environment assumptions.

Problem addressed:

Locate execution-specific dependencies and challenge static hypotheses.

Failure mode:

A slice for an observed execution is treated as covering unobserved executions.

Mechanism:

Trace a relevant execution and its data/control effects to answer a bounded question, retaining the input, environment and observation criterion.

Trigger context:

Observed behaviour or a concrete failure requires an execution-specific explanation.

Non trigger cheap path:

Use direct reproduction or existing logs when adequate; omit instrumentation when no relevant run can be obtained.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • Reproducible or adequately characterised execution; instrumentation does not conceal or change the critical effect.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

Static uncertainty, dynamic dispatch or a reproducible failure makes execution evidence discriminating. Select the question needed for a proposed change, diagnosis or handover rather than presupposing whole-system understanding.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Trace, instrumentation, inputs and runtime configuration. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

Preservation obligation and observer

The observed run and selected values/events. Distinguish a recovered description from an authorised requirement and from what an actual user can observe.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Static relations overapproximate modelled paths; dynamic traces underapproximate possible executions; fuse only with declared boundaries.

Comprehension assumptions

Reproducible or adequately characterised execution; instrumentation does not conceal or change the critical effect. Incomplete intent, unsupported languages, generated code and tacit operational knowledge limit recovery.

Oracle and regression limits

Recovered models require cross-checking; observed behaviour can be a defect and absent evidence is not evidence of absence.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

Recovery may reveal interface or migration assumptions but cannot itself establish their validity.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

Read-only inquiry normally needs no production rollback; intrusive instrumentation must control perturbation and cleanup.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Maintainers and domain/operational experts exchange concrete questions and evidence; documentation is useful through an actual consumer.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

A debugger or targeted log can suffice; do not collect exhaustive production traces without need. Stop inquiry when it discriminates the pending decision sufficiently; deepen it when contradictions or impact escape appear; retire stale views.

Problem addressed:

Reduce repeated rediscovery and misleading handovers.

Failure mode:

Recovered documents are produced or maintained without a consumer or actionable knowledge payoff.

Mechanism:

Produce or refresh a description only when a maintainer or downstream consumer needs it, and check it against the current subject.

Trigger context:

A useful explanation is missing, stale or inaccessible to an actual consumer.

Non trigger cheap path:

A checked example, code comment or targeted note can replace a large document.

Dependencies preconditions:

Conditions

  • A resolvable source baseline and a way to detect stale statements.

Related property ids

  • ESME-C005

  • ESME-C013

  • ESME-C070

Interpretation

Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

Domain profile:

Change intent and change class

A useful explanation is missing, stale or inaccessible to an actual consumer. Select the question needed for a proposed change, diagnosis or handover rather than presupposing whole-system understanding.

Baseline and affected artefacts

Documentation and its source artefact/version. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

Preservation obligation and observer

The intended reader performing a named maintenance or operational task. Distinguish a recovered description from an authorised requirement and from what an actual user can observe.

Impact boundary and dependency evidence

Static relations overapproximate modelled paths; dynamic traces underapproximate possible executions; fuse only with declared boundaries.

Comprehension assumptions

A resolvable source baseline and a way to detect stale statements. Incomplete intent, unsupported languages, generated code and tacit operational knowledge limit recovery.

Oracle and regression limits

Recovered models require cross-checking; observed behaviour can be a defect and absent evidence is not evidence of absence.

Compatibility and migration preconditions

Recovery may reveal interface or migration assumptions but cannot itself establish their validity.

Release rollback or forward repair condition

Read-only inquiry normally needs no production rollback; intrusive instrumentation must control perturbation and cleanup.

Maintainer and downstream consumers

Maintainers and domain/operational experts exchange concrete questions and evidence; documentation is useful through an actual consumer.

Lifecycle cost and retirement condition

A checked example, code comment or targeted note can replace a large document. Stop inquiry when it discriminates the pending decision sufficiently; deepen it when contradictions or impact escape appear; retire stale views.

The input-scoped variants below supplement the canonical formulation only under their own triggers; they are alternatives/facets, not a universal conjunction of all controls.
